text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Fatherland Union submitted a draft law to the parliament calling for a referendum on the Estonian-Russian border agreement. The draft has been worded to avoid conflict with the constitution, which does not permit referenda on international agreements.

- Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin promised President Lennart Meri in Lisbon that Russia will not delay the signing of the border agreement and Meri is hopeful to have it signed early next year.
- The Reform party declared its firm opposition to a planned protective customs tariffs.
- The Finance ministry increased the draft budget by 100 million kroons on presumed revenues from the sales tax in 1997.
- The Estonian Security Police has started an investigation on suspected bribing of a judge by a popular attorney. The lawyer has not been named.
- The public share offer of the state-owned company Estonian Gas will begin in May.
- The culture ministry work group intends to merge the Estonian radio and TV into Estonian Broadcasting. The draft laws will be debated early next year.
- The German chemical company Goldschmidt AG has agreed to dispose of hazardous industrial waste imported to Estonia in 1992 by the firm's predecessor.
